semantic_differences.stopping_nmflib: every iteration: |F_t - F_{t-1}| / max(1, |F_{t-1}|) < tol, where F is the full regularized objective (1/2||V-WH||_F^2 or KL, plus Omega)
semantic_differences.stopping_sklearn_cd: every iteration: KKT violation / violation_init <= tol (violation_init measured after iteration 1); break if violation_init==0
semantic_differences.stopping_sklearn_mu: every 10 iterations: (previous_error - error)/error_at_init < tol, error = ||X-WH||_F for frobenius, sqrt(2*KL) for kullback-leibler; regularization is NOT part of this monitored error
semantic_differences.update_order: NMFlib MU/CD update H first then W; sklearn MU updates W first then H (CD: W then H as well). Same alternating scheme, different path.
semantic_differences.kl_zero_protection: sklearn MU-KL floors WH at EPSILON=1.1920929e-07 (float32 eps) inside the V/WH ratio, maps zero W column sums to 1.0 and zero denominators to EPSILON, and zeroes H entries below float64 eps after updates; V>0 with WH=0 therefore yields a large finite ratio instead of an error. NMFlib returns NumericalError for V>0 and WH=0, normalizes zero-denominator components to 0, and never adds epsilon to the KL objective itself.
semantic_differences.random_init: both use scale sqrt(mean(V)/k); sklearn draws |standard_normal| (half-normal, numpy RNG), NMFlib draws uniform(0,1) (SplitMix64). Same integer seed does NOT give the same initial W/H.
semantic_differences.nndsvd: sklearn nndsvd/nndsvda use randomized SVD (depends on random_state); NMFlib uses deterministic internal power iteration + deflation (seed-independent). Element-wise equality is not expected.
semantic_differences.converged_field: NMFlib exposes converged(); sklearn NMF has NO converged attribute, only n_iter_. sklearn rows record converged as empty and hit_max_iter = (n_iter_ >= max_iter).
semantic_differences.reconstruction_err_: sklearn reconstruction_err_ = _beta_divergence(X,W,H,beta_loss,square_root=True): ||X-WH||_F for frobenius loss but sqrt(2*KL) for kullback-leibler loss (both solvers). NMFlib reconstruction_error is ALWAYS ||V-WH||_F regardless of loss. Independent evaluation uses the Frobenius norm for both sides; sklearn's reported value is crosschecked against its own documented semantics.

nmflib_fit_seconds_note: per-fit timing is not exposed by the NMFlib public API; only the total runner wall time is recorded (no production change made)
reproducibility_note: verified empirically with two consecutive full-grid runs: all results.csv columns are bit-identical except fit_seconds (sklearn per-fit wall timings) and moonbit_runner_wall_seconds here, which are inherently nondeterministic; datasets, parameters, factors, objectives and crosschecks reproduce exactly
crosscheck_rule: fail if rel > 1e-8 AND abs > 1e-9 (cancellation near zero)
